name: Syndactyly type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and genetic diagnosis of Syndactyly type 2

criteria.description: Presence of cutaneous and/or bony syndactyly primarily affecting the third and fourth fingers and/or fourth and fifth toes
Associated presence of postaxial polydactyly (extra digits) in hands or feet
Identification of pathogenic variants in the HOXD13 gene
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Radiographic evidence of bony fusion or duplication of phalanges

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic syndactyly and polydactyly with genetic confirmation of HOXD13 mutation or consistent family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for confirmation due to phenotypic overlap with other syndactyly types.

common.symptomName: Symphalangism affecting the phalanges of the hand

imaging: Radiographs showing bony fusion or duplication of phalanges
genetic: Pathogenic variants in HOXD13 gene identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic syndactyly and polydactyly pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Syndactyly type 1 typically involves fusion of second and third fingers without polydactyly
Presence of congenital scalp defects (aplasia cutis)
Syndactyly accompanied by skin absence, not typical in syndactyly type 2

redFlags: Severe functional impairment of hand due to extensive bony fusion
Presence of developmental delay suggesting syndromic association
Recurrent infections in webbed areas indicating skin breakdown
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
